## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Yāna Sikkhāpada* ("Rule on traveling in a vehicle"), designated as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 85, is an expiation rule within the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who rides or travels in a vehicle commits an offence requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. The text is translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this prohibition was standard across early Buddhist monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. It corresponds directly to the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-pc85*), Bhikkhunī Parivāra Pācittiya 85, and relates to Khandhaka 20 (Bhikkhunikkhandhaka) [SuttaCentral]. Cross-tradition parallels include the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 159*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 141*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 145*), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese *Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 158* and Tibetan *xct-mu-bi-vb-pc132*), and Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda (Chinese *Lzh Mg Bi Vb Pc 111* and Sanskrit *san-lo-bi-vb-pc111*) [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus align with this cross-lineage distribution, matching segments against the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and *Prātimokṣasūtra*, as well as Tibetan versions in the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) and the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīprātimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 374 matching passages across 90 texts, sharing substantial legal and narrative formulas most notably with adjacent and related Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules such as Pācittiya 84 (§0.1–2.1.5), Pāṭidesanīya 1 (§1.1.5–1.1.14.1), and Pāṭidesanīya 2–8 [DharmaNexus].
